desktop_mission.mission_sub: Multi-Slit Angular Dispersion, Atomic Emission Lines & Resolving Power
desktop_mission.voice_mission: Today we're simulating a diffraction grating spectrometer and atomic emission lines in Kotlin.
math_cards: Constructive interference across thousands of periodic slits produces sharp angular peaks
Angular separation between adjacent spectral lines scales directly with ruling density
Rayleigh criterion resolution limit scales with harmonic order and total illuminated grooves
desktop_mission.voice_math: The core physics: the grating diffraction equation, angular dispersion rate, and chromatic resolving power.

math_steps.formula: d · sin(θ_m) = m · λ  (θ_m = asin(m · λ / d))
math_steps.note: Constructive interference occurs when path lengths between adjacent slits differ by integer wavelengths
math_steps.code:
// 1. Grating equation: angular deflection for m-th diffraction order
val grooveSpacingNm = 1_000_000f / linesPerMm
val sinTheta = (orderM * wavelengthNm) / grooveSpacingNm
val isDiffracted = abs(sinTheta) <= 1.0f
val thetaRad = if (isDiffracted) asin(sinTheta) else 0f
math_steps.sub_desc: Computes angular deflection angle for each spectral order.

math_steps.formula: y_m = L · tan(θ_m),  D = dθ / dλ = m / (d · cos(θ_m))
math_steps.note: Higher ruling densities and orders spread spectral lines further apart across the detector screen
math_steps.sub_desc: Calculates screen focal spot position and wavelength separation gradient.

math_steps.formula: R = λ / Δλ = m · N_total,  I(θ) = I_0 · [sin(N·β) / sin(β)]²
math_steps.note: Thousands of coherent micro-slits narrow broad interference fringes into razor-sharp atomic peaks
math_steps.code:
// 3. Multi-slit chromatic resolving power and peak interference intensity
val resolvingPower = orderM * totalGrooveCount
val beta = (PI.toFloat() * grooveSpacingNm * sin(thetaRad)) / wavelengthNm
val intensityFactor = if (abs(sin(beta)) < 1e-3f) 1f else (sin(numSlitsActive * beta) / (numSlitsActive * sin(beta))).pow(2)
math_steps.sub_desc: Evaluates Rayleigh resolution limit and multi-slit intensity sharpness.
